summary: Siegbert Hummel (1908–2001) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tübingen, Rostock, Munich, and Leipzig (PhD), working under Eduard Erkes, Johannes Schubert, André Wedemeyer, and Friedrich Weller. He was curator at the Grassi Museum (1947–1955).

Siegfried Behrsing (1903–1994) worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Greifswald, Tübingen, and Leipzig (PhD), learning under Heller, Zimmer, Garbe, Hauer, Ochler, Haas, Weller, Haenisch, Conrady, and Hertel. He held posts at Leipzig, Berlin's Ethnological Museum, and Humboldt University.

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin, Tübingen (PhD), Göttingen, and Paris under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and Theodor Benfey. He later served as professor at the University of Strasbourg.

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist. He studied at Vienna (Dr. phil.), Paris, and Stockholm (Habilitation). He held academic posts at Banaras Hindu University, Göttingen, Kiel, and Stockholm University, and served as Secretary General of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Sieglinde Dietz (born 1944) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Bonn, completing her PhD under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Frank-Richard Hamm. In 1990, she held an attested post at Göttingen University.

Siew-Yue Killingley (1940–2004) was a linguist. She earned an MA from the University of Malaya and a PhD from SOAS University of London. She lectured in linguistics at St Mary's College, Fenham, and taught linguistics and Chinese at Newcastle University.

Sigmund Feist (1865–1943) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Heinrich Hübschmann at the University of Strasbourg, where he completed his PhD in 1888. From 1906 to 1935, he was director of the Reichenheim Orphanage.
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied under Ludo Rocher and serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar of religious studies and other fields. She studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford, and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Sigrid Westphal-Hellbusch (1915–1984) worked in Indology and other fields. After earning her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin, she held positions there, at Museum Fünf Kontinente, the Free University of Berlin, and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

Sigurd Lindquist (1895–1943) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Karl Ferdinand Johansson at Uppsala University, completing his PhD in 1932, and became a docent there in 1934.

Silvia Luraghi (born 1958) is a linguist and Indologist. She earned a Laurea from the University of Turin and a PhD in linguistics from the University of Pavia, later holding posts at Turin, Roma Tre, and Pavia.
Silvio Trovanelli was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied law at the University of Bologna until 1883 and later served there as a docent of juridical philosophy.

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held positions at Naples "L'Orientale", Naples Federico II, Sapienza University, Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Simo Parpola (born 1943) is a linguist and historian-archaeologist. Educated at Helsinki (PhD), the Pontifical Biblical Institute, and the British Museum, he held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and Helsinki, with visiting positions at Padua and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Simon Cubelic is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Heidelberg and an MA at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Heidelberg University, before posts at Munich and the Göttingen Academy.

Simon Matthews Edwin Kempson (1831–1892) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Cheltenham College and Gonville and Caius College. He served as headmaster at Bareilly College, taught at the University of Cambridge, and was Professor of Hindustani at Camberley.
Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has served as a tutor and later as a lecturer in the Department of Philosophy at Durham University.
Simon Winant is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He is attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Simon Wong is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts in Dermatology and Skin Science at the University of British Columbia and as a professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
